correctness.rationale: The incidence model and its supplied map to the Pappus LCF graph agree. An independent replay exhausts point-to-line bijections with the incidence restriction and constructs triples from disjoint perfect matchings and their complements. Direct enumeration of named edge assignments independently checks the state count. For each pair of colors every connected component of their union is an alternating cycle, so enumerating all such switches and discarding global renaming loops exhausts the moves on the quotient. Replay confirms 42 perfect matchings, 20 unordered states (120 named), 36 edges, two opposite-product-sign components each with one universal hub and three disjoint peripheral triangles, and the claimed cycle profiles. Switching a 2k-cycle multiplies the sign of each of the two matching bijections by the same (−1)^(k−1), proving invariance; the computed components prove sufficiency and diameter two. Relabeling either ordered bipartition may flip the overall sign convention, not the sign partition.
residual_risks: Exhaustive for this graph and the quotient by global color names. Sign sufficiency and the windmill form are not claims for arbitrary bipartite cubic graphs.

value.rationale: For the natural Pappus graph a genuinely unknown full switch graph would be useful beyond knowing a class count: it resolves class sizes, cliques and worst-case distance. In this submission the precise finite object is already available in the distinct published match. The marginal sign label follows from the two known components, the standard matching sign invariant and one explicit reflection; the other marginal counts follow from known profiles. The package does not furnish a scientifically valuable distinct remainder to repair.
residual_risks: This is a judgment about added scientific content relative to verified coverage, not a claim that finite switch graphs lack value.
